about: Column alignment table for convert: one chord line in, one line out, Roman style.
Derived by hand from the Column alignment requirement of the chord-conversion spec, not by running convert:
a unit (a run of glued tokens) starts at the source column of its first token; when the output before it
already reaches that column it is put exactly one space after the previous unit; a gap that contains a tab
is copied unchanged and columns are counted afresh from the unit after it; leading and trailing whitespace
are copied. Rows are [key, input, expected, what the row shows]. `\t` is a tab.
rows: Gap with a tab is copied
a later chord returns to its source column once there is room
a shift carries only as far as it has to
a shorter chord leaves a wider gap, so the next one keeps its column
a header keeps its text and its column
markers keep their text and their columns
a parenthesised chord is one unit
a chord and its comma are one unit
a footnote star stays on its chord
a long dash-joined unit pushes the next unit one space off
after a tab, columns are counted from the unit that follows it
after a tab, an unchanged width keeps the following gap
a gap of spaces and a tab is copied whole
a longer chord uses up the gap after it before it moves its neighbour
accidentals and slash basses lengthen a chord like any suffix
